subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, with this PR's no-override defaults and `standard` versus `full` hook-extra semantics?
rationale: The code path is bounded, but choosing a new prompt-context config/default contract affects compatibility, session context, docs, and overlapping bootstrap-control proposals in a way automation should not decide alone.

options.title: Sponsor This PR Shape
options.body: Proceed with this additive config surface after requiring public docs and final review of no-override, explicit-tier, and hook-extra behavior.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Bootstrap Policy
options.body: Pause this PR and resolve the tiering request inside a broader bootstrap/session-selection design such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46565.

options.title: Decline The New Config Knob
options.body: Keep current fixed bootstrap filtering and steer users to existing context injection, budget, and lightweight-context controls instead.

recommendation.title: Sponsor This PR Shape
recommendation.body: Proceed with this additive config surface after requiring public docs and final review of no-override, explicit-tier, and hook-extra behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review context and subagent bootstrap feature history make this the best available product/API decision owner.
